title: Who Held the Pen
concept: Two UAA professors say Anthropic's Claude wrote the first draft of the University of Alaska's 'AI Engaged' plan, which the Board of Regents is set to take up at its November meeting. The university's technology chief says he drafted it over the summer at the regents' request, and we found no university response to the Claude claim. A UAA report says 119 of 150 students cited for misconduct used AI and AI plagiarism rose 73% last year. The fair case: a university official says AI could recommend but a human decides. The film's position is that who held the pen matters less than who was consulted, because by the reporting the summer draft got too little faculty and student feedback. A DiplomaPress with a mint machine handle and an oxblood human examiner handle is the hero and the draft sheet is the throughline, ending unsigned before two dark chairs

fingerprint.palette: burgundy and oak seminar room at dusk, cream sheets, an oxblood brass press, mint machine light and highlighter yellow
fingerprint.metaphor: a plan-stamping press with a machine handle and a human handle, and a draft sheet that changes state until it lies unsigned before two dark chairs

palette: burgundy and oak seminar room at dusk, cream sheets, an oxblood brass press, mint machine light and highlighter yellow
divergence_note: The last films were an indigo night cab (11-02), a storm slate slope (11-01), a sage chart desk (10-31) and an aubergine depot (10-29). This film is a warm burgundy and oak seminar room at dusk with cream paper, a mint machine glow and highlighter yellow light. Its hero is an oxblood brass credential press, and it has no cab, slope, chart desk or depot. The throughline is the AI ENGAGED draft sheet, which changes state at every act boundary.

treatment.title: The Press With Two Handles
treatment.summary: Explainer's mechanism (machine handle vs human handle) with the Dramatist's empty chairs and the Comedian's pen between two hands, and the Enthusiast's fair case given a full scene.

angle.thesis: A plan that says a human decides is being judged on who held the pen. The drafting tool matters less than whether faculty and students were in the room, and by the reporting the summer draft had too little of their feedback.
angle.falsifiable_by: A record that faculty and students were consulted before the draft was written, or a UA statement that no AI drafted the text and the plan was reviewed line by line by people (c3 c8 c11).
supporting_facts: c3 UA technology chief drafted it over the summer
c8 too little faculty and student feedback
c2 c4 professors say Claude drafted, disclosed Oct 9th
angle.counterpoint: Using an AI to draft is not itself a flaw. The plan's own rule is a human decides (c9), the cheating numbers are real (c5 c6) and the UA response was not found (c11). Honored as the TEST act: the fair case gets its own scene at full strength.
runner_ups: Senate race AI donor money (lost: campaign finance, secondary only)
Fairbanks town hall (lost: overlaps excluded data-center subject)
